nodes.label: [TSD001] CAN Bus Attack (Message Spoofing, Flooding, Replay)
nodes.name: CAN Bus Attack (Message Spoofing, Flooding, Replay)
nodes.description: Adversary gains access to the CAN bus to inject malicious messages, disrupt communication by flooding the bus, or replay old messages. This can lead to incorrect battery state reporting (SoC/SoH), false commands (e.g., contactor status), or denial of service.

data.label: [TSD001] CAN Bus Attack (Message Spoofing, Flooding, Replay)

nodes.label: Message Spoofing
nodes.name: Message Spoofing
nodes.description: Adversary crafts and injects fake CAN messages to deceive the BMS, leading to incorrect state estimations or control actions.

nodes.label: Inject Malicious CAN Frame
nodes.name: Inject Malicious CAN Frame
nodes.description: MITRE ATT&CK T1050: Application Window Discovery. Adversary directly injects manipulated CAN frames into the bus.

nodes.label: Message Flooding
nodes.name: Message Flooding
nodes.description: Adversary overwhelms the CAN bus with excessive messages, causing a denial of service for legitimate communication.

nodes.label: Generate High Volume CAN Traffic
nodes.name: Generate High Volume CAN Traffic
nodes.description: MITRE ATT&CK T1499: Network Service Scanning. Adversary floods the bus with legitimate or malformed CAN frames.

nodes.label: Replay Attack
nodes.name: Replay Attack
nodes.description: Adversary captures legitimate CAN messages and retransmits them later to achieve unintended actions or bypass security checks.

nodes.label: Capture Legitimate CAN Frame
nodes.name: Capture Legitimate CAN Frame
nodes.description: Adversary monitors CAN bus to capture relevant messages.

nodes.label: Re-transmit Captured Frame
nodes.name: Re-transmit Captured Frame
nodes.description: Adversary injects the captured frame at a later time.

nodes.label: [TSD002] Debug Port Attack (JTAG/SWD Exploitation)
nodes.name: Debug Port Attack (JTAG/SWD Exploitation)
nodes.description: Adversary gains physical or logical access to debug interfaces (e.g., JTAG, SWD) to extract sensitive information, tamper with firmware, or gain control of the ECU. This can compromise confidentiality of keys and certificates, integrity of code, and availability of the system.

nodes.label: Data Extraction
nodes.name: Data Extraction
nodes.description: Adversary uses debug interfaces to read out sensitive information like keys, certificates, or firmware.

nodes.label: Read Memory via Debug Interface
nodes.name: Read Memory via Debug Interface
nodes.description: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. Accessing memory contents through JTAG/SWD.

nodes.label: Firmware Tampering
nodes.name: Firmware Tampering
nodes.description: Adversary overwrites or modifies the ECU's firmware through debug interfaces.

nodes.label: Write Flash Memory via Debug Interface
nodes.name: Write Flash Memory via Debug Interface
nodes.description: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation. Modifying firmware stored in Code Flash or Data Flash.

data.label: Write Flash Memory via Debug Interface

nodes.label: Glitching Attacks
nodes.name: Glitching Attacks
nodes.description: Adversary uses voltage or clock glitches to induce faults and bypass security mechanisms.

nodes.label: Voltage Glitching
nodes.name: Voltage Glitching
nodes.description: CWE-1247: Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches. Inducing transient voltage fluctuations.

nodes.label: Clock Glitching
nodes.name: Clock Glitching
nodes.description: CWE-1247: Improper Protection Against Voltage and Clock Glitches. Modifying clock signal frequency or timing.

nodes.label: [TSD003] Data Flash Attack (Modification/Exfiltration)
nodes.name: Data Flash Attack (Modification/Exfiltration)
nodes.description: Adversary targets the Data Flash to modify critical parameters, logs (like SoH), or exfiltrate sensitive data. This can impact battery performance, warranty claims, and data integrity.

nodes.label: Parameter Modification
nodes.name: Parameter Modification
nodes.description: Adversary alters stored parameters in Data Flash, impacting battery management logic and potentially causing safety issues.

nodes.label: Write to Data Flash
nodes.name: Write to Data Flash
nodes.description: ATM Technique: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Persistence. Writing malicious data or code to Data Flash.

nodes.label: Data Exfiltration
nodes.name: Data Exfiltration
nodes.description: Adversary reads sensitive data from Data Flash, such as battery usage logs or configuration data.

nodes.label: Read from Data Flash
nodes.name: Read from Data Flash
nodes.description: ATM Technique: Abuse Standard Diagnostic Protocol for Collection. Reading stored battery health data or logs.

nodes.label: [TSD004] Internet Communication Attack (C&C, Data Exfiltration)
nodes.name: Internet Communication Attack (C&C, Data Exfiltration)
nodes.description: Adversary exploits the internet connection of the BMS (if applicable, e.g., via connected vehicle services) for command and control or to exfiltrate sensitive battery data.

nodes.label: Command and Control (C2)
nodes.name: Command and Control (C2)
nodes.description: Adversary uses the internet connection to send commands to the BMS or control other vehicle functions.

nodes.label: Receive Commands Remotely
nodes.name: Receive Commands Remotely
nodes.description: ATM Technique: Internet Communication. Adversary sends commands via the internet connection to control the BMS.

nodes.label: Data Exfiltration
nodes.name: Data Exfiltration
nodes.description: Adversary transmits sensitive battery data (e.g., usage patterns, health status) to an external server.

nodes.label: Send Battery Data Externally
nodes.name: Send Battery Data Externally
nodes.description: ATM Technique: Internet Communication. Exfiltrating battery data over the internet connection.

scenes.Name: Secure Onboard Communication (SecOC)
scenes.Description: Implement SecOC for critical CAN messages to ensure message authentication and integrity.

scenes.Name: CAN Controller Hardware Filtering
scenes.Description: Configure CAN controllers to filter messages by ID at the hardware level, accepting only whitelisted IDs.

scenes.Name: Rate Limiting on CAN Messages
scenes.Description: Implement rate limiting to detect and discard excessive message traffic on the CAN bus.

scenes.Name: JTAG/Debug Port Lockout
scenes.Description: Disable or protect debug ports (JTAG/SWD) after manufacturing using OTP fuses or challenge-response mechanisms.

scenes.Name: Hardware Security Module (HSM)
scenes.Description: Utilize an HSM to protect cryptographic keys and certificates, preventing extraction via debug interfaces or side-channels.

scenes.Name: Memory Protection Unit (MPU)
scenes.Description: Configure MPU to isolate critical code and data segments, preventing unauthorized access or modification through debug interfaces.

scenes.Name: Secure Boot
scenes.Description: Implement secure boot to verify the integrity and authenticity of firmware before execution, preventing execution of tampered code from Data Flash.

scenes.Name: Secure Storage (NVM)
scenes.Description: Encrypt sensitive data stored in Data Flash and use monotonic counters to prevent rollback attacks on logs like SoH.

scenes.Name: Diagnostic Authentication
scenes.Description: Enforce strong authentication for privileged diagnostic services to prevent unauthorized access and modification of Data Flash contents.

scenes.Name: Secure Communication Channel (TLS/DTLS)
scenes.Description: Utilize secure communication protocols (e.g., TLS/DTLS) for any internet-connected services to protect data confidentiality and integrity.

scenes.Name: Network Segmentation
scenes.Description: If possible, segment the network to isolate the BMS from other less secure components, limiting the impact of internet-borne threats.

scenes.Name: Intrusion Detection System (IDS)
scenes.Description: Implement an IDS to monitor network traffic for anomalous patterns indicative of C&C or data exfiltration attempts over the internet connection.

scenes.Name: E2E Protection (Internal)
scenes.Description: Apply End-to-End protection on SPI communication between the MCU and Cell Monitors to detect data corruption or tampering.

scenes.Name: Data Integrity Checks
scenes.Description: Implement checksums or CRCs for critical data transmitted over IO and CAN interfaces to detect corruption.

scenes.Name: Defensive Coding Practices
scenes.Description: Follow secure coding standards (e.g., MISRA C) to prevent vulnerabilities that could be exploited via debug interfaces or by tampering with firmware.
